scope: execution-required KVM qga later-reboot autostart recovery check

findings.command: sc qc QEMU-GA; sc query QEMU-GA
findings.guest_result: A later retained reboot showed the service still configured as `START_TYPE : 2 AUTO_START` and already in `STATE : 4 RUNNING`.

findings.command: virsh qemu-agent-command ...; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --pretty '{"execute":"query-chardev"}'; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --hmp 'info qtree'; direct AF_UNIX connect
findings.host_result: Despite the later automatic service recovery, `guest-ping` still returned `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error`, `query-chardev` still showed `frontend-open=true`, `info qtree` still showed `guest on, host off`, and direct host-side connect to the qga unix socket still returned `Connection refused`.

findings.command: journalctl --since '15 minutes ago' | rg 'failed to connect to agent socket|Cannot connect to QEMU guest agent|available due to an error|not connected'
findings.host_result: The retained host journal now also contains `virtqemud` lines for `failed to connect to agent socket: Connection refused` and `Cannot connect to QEMU guest agent for regprobe-win11-25h2-session`, matching the direct socket probe.

conclusion: The earlier boot-time qga service crash is retained but no longer looks deterministic. A later reboot recovered the Windows service under ordinary `AUTO_START`, yet the host-side attach failure persisted unchanged.
